scenes.title: The slope between two points
narration: How steep is a curve at a particular point? Let's look at the function: f of x equals one half times x squared.
First we connect two points on the curve. This line is called a secant. Its slope is the difference in height divided by the horizontal distance.

scenes.title: The second point moves closer
narration: Point A stays at x equals one. Now the second point B moves along the curve, closer and closer to A. As it does, the secant turns.
Its slope approaches the value one here. The secant approaches the tangent. So what happens to the secant?

scenes.title: The derivative is a slope
narration: When the slopes of the secants approach the same value from both sides, we get the derivative. It is the slope of the tangent at this point.
For our function, the derivative at x equals one is exactly one. If we go one unit to the right along the tangent, we go one unit up.

scenes.title: Up close, the curve looks almost straight
narration: Let's zoom in around point A. The curve and its tangent lie closer and closer together. In this small section, the curve looks almost like a straight line.
The derivative describes this local slope. It does not describe an area, and not a highest point either. What does the derivative at a point tell you?
